acceptance_criteria.text: `devflow telemetry metrics` with no `--issue` prints exactly the same JSON keys and values as before: spans, synthetic_spans_excluded, ticket_turn_outcomes, agent_cli_calls, coding_cost_usd_recorded, stage_latency_seconds. A regression test compares this against a fixed log.
`devflow telemetry metrics --issue N` parses as an integer. N below 1 or a non-integer exits non-zero with an `error:` message, like the existing replay `--limit` validation.

With `--issue N`, only spans in the session `<repo>:issue-N` are counted. Spans from other issues are excluded, including issue 12 when N is 1. Spans from synthetic traces, such as `devflow-connectivity-demo` or those with `langfuse.trace.metadata.synthetic == "true"`, are excluded and counted under `synthetic_spans_excluded`.

For an issue with several `ticket.run` spans in the same session (resumes), the output has one summary for that session with `runs` equal to the number of `ticket.run` spans. Outcomes are counted per `devflow.result`, falling back to span status as the existing code does.

The per-ticket summary reports `active_run_seconds`, the sum of `ticket.run` span durations with overlapping intervals merged. It reports `elapsed_wall_seconds`, from the earliest `ticket.run` start to the latest `ticket.run` end. It reports `inferred_gap_seconds`, which is elapsed wall time minus active run time and never negative. Field names or an explicit labels object mark the first two as observed span time and the third as inferred between invocations.

The per-ticket summary reports stage duration summaries (count, mean, max) for `stage.*` spans excluding `stage.result`. It reports agent duration summaries (count, mean, max) for `agent.*` spans, keyed by agent and role from the span name. It also reports counts of agent calls.

The output contains only counts, durations, outcome names and span names. It never includes `langfuse.observation.input` or `langfuse.observation.output`, prompt hashes, agent session ids or any other attribute values. A test with a captured-content log asserts that none of that text appears in stdout.
An empty or missing log, or a log with no spans for the issue, with `--issue N` exits 0. It prints a valid JSON summary with zero counts and null or zero durations, and does not raise.
Malformed JSON lines in the log are skipped as today. The `--issue` path does not crash on records that lack optional fields such as `end_ns` or `attributes`.
`ruff check .` and `python -m pytest` pass. The new tests cover empty log, unrelated issues, resumed runs, synthetic traces, privacy and no-argument compatibility. No existing test is weakened.

follow_ups.title: Make `telemetry metrics` tolerate non-object or incomplete trace records
follow_ups.why: The existing aggregate loop does `record["name"]` and `record["attributes"]` on whatever `json.loads` returns. A valid-JSON line that is not an object, or one missing those keys, raises and aborts the command (a KeyError is reported as `error:` with exit 2).

plan.goal: Add an optional `--issue N` filter to `devflow telemetry metrics` that reports a per-ticket latency summary for that issue's Langfuse session. The summary combines all resumed invocations and separates observed span time from inferred gaps. Output with no `--issue` stays unchanged.
out_of_scope: Changing what spans are emitted or which attributes they carry, including making `devflow.issue` propagate to child spans
Querying the Langfuse API or OTLP collector; this reads the local `traces.jsonl` only
Changing `devflow stats` or the workflow database
Per-ticket summaries in no-argument output, which stays exactly as it is today
Cost or token reporting per issue
Changing replay, demo or status behaviour
risks: The output shape for `--issue` is new and not specified in detail by the ticket. The plan defaults to the existing aggregate keys over the filtered records plus a `sessions` list, so callers can add fields later without breaking it.

The session id embeds the repo name (`<repo>:issue-N`). If a trace log is shared between repos, matching on the `:issue-N` suffix could merge two repos' sessions. Group by the full session id and report each session separately instead of merging by suffix.

Elapsed wall time covers only the first recorded run start to the last recorded run end. Human wait time before the first run or after the last is not observable, and the gap between runs is an inference, not a measurement. The labels must say so.
Overlapping `ticket.run` spans from concurrent invocations could double-count active time. Merge intervals to avoid this.
Rounding and float arithmetic on nanosecond timestamps can make tests flaky. Use values that are exact multiples of 1e9 ns, or compare with approx.

steps.description: Add the `--issue` option (type int, default None) to the `metrics` parser only. It must not appear on status, replay or demo. Keep `path` as the optional positional argument.

In `telemetry_cli.py`, move the aggregate computation into a helper with unchanged behaviour. Leave the no-`--issue` code path producing byte-identical output. Add `issue_summary(records, issue)` as a separate pure function that is easy to unit test. It selects non-synthetic records whose `langfuse.session.id` ends with `:issue-<N>` or whose `langfuse.trace.metadata.issue`/`devflow.issue` equals N. It matches the exact issue number so `issue-1` does not match `issue-12`. It groups by `langfuse.session.id`.

Implement the per-session summary inside `issue_summary`. It computes run count and outcome counts from `ticket.run` spans, active run seconds via merged intervals, elapsed wall seconds, inferred gap seconds, stage duration stats and agent duration stats. Round to 3 decimals like the existing output. It reads only whitelisted fields (name, start_ns, end_ns, status, `devflow.result`, session id) and never copies attribute values into the output. Guard against missing or invalid timestamps.

Wire `--issue` into `command()`. Validate N >= 1 and raise ValueError otherwise. Print the aggregate keys computed over the filtered records, plus a `sessions` list (or equivalent) holding the per-ticket summary. Handle a missing log and an issue with no spans by printing zeroed output with exit 0. Document the output shape in the code via the field names and a short `labels`/`notes` entry for observed versus inferred time.

Add tests in a new file that writes synthetic JSONL logs to a tmp git repo and runs `main(["telemetry","metrics",...])` with `capsys`, or calls the helper directly. Cover empty/missing log, unrelated issue and prefix collision (1 vs 12), resumed runs across two traces with a gap, overlapping spans, demo/synthetic traces excluded, privacy (content attributes absent from stdout), malformed lines, and the unchanged no-argument output. Use the existing telemetry/CLI test fixtures and `tmp_path` repo setup; look at `tests/conftest.py` for helpers.
Document `--issue N`, the session grouping, active versus elapsed versus inferred-gap semantics, and the privacy guarantee. Add an example to the README telemetry snippet.
Run `ruff check .` and `python -m pytest` and fix any failures without altering unrelated tests.

acceptance_criteria.text: The ticket.run root span carries trace metadata with the repository name and the ticket's base SHA. The keys are langfuse.trace.metadata.base_sha and devflow.base_sha, plus a sanitized remote identity (host/owner/repo) when the repo has one. The base SHA is set on first run, after worktree creation, and on resumed runs from ticket.base_sha. Child spans created after that point inherit it.

After each graph freshness check made for an agent request, the ticket trace carries the graph status and a short fingerprint. The status is one of fresh, refreshed, failed or unavailable. The fingerprint is a truncated hex string, or empty when the tree is not a git repo. Node and edge counts are included only as integers when known. The latest check wins.

Each graph.refresh span has explicit attributes: devflow.graph.refreshed (bool; true only when a rebuild actually succeeded), devflow.graph.status, devflow.graph.nodes, devflow.graph.edges, devflow.graph.fingerprint. A no-op check on an up-to-date graph gives refreshed=false, status=fresh and the existing counts. A rebuild gives refreshed=true, status=refreshed and the new counts. A rebuild that ran but failed gives status=failed, refreshed=false, with counts of 0 and no counts presented as fresh.

A missing graphify binary, a failed build, a non-git directory, or a graph builder that raises an exception gives status=unavailable or failed. The ticket continues to run and the agent request is still built (the digest already says 'Code graph: unavailable'). No exception from the graph step propagates out of Engine._request.

Metadata uses only allowlisted keys. Values are validated (SHAs and fingerprints match a hex regex, status comes from a fixed enum, counts are ints, remote has any userinfo, query and fragment stripped). Nothing from prompts, issue text, file paths, graph contents, error messages or credentials is added. The metadata is emitted in both metadata-only and capture_content modes.

New tests cover fresh, refreshed, failed and unavailable graph states at the graphctx/span level, and at least the unavailable and refreshed states at the full ticket level. They also check base_sha equals the stored ticket.base_sha, that a raising builder does not break the run, and that a remote URL with embedded credentials never appears in the trace log.
`ruff check .` and `python -m pytest` pass with no existing test weakened, skipped or deleted. docs/observability.md documents the new metadata and graph.refresh attributes.

follow_ups.title: Make GraphStatus.refreshed accurate when a rebuild fails
follow_ups.why: ensure_fresh returns GraphStatus(result.ran, False, ...) on a failed build, so `refreshed` is true even though nothing was refreshed. This plan works around it with an explicit state field, but the field itself is misleading to other callers.

follow_ups.title: Guard the retro-time graph refresh in Engine._learn against builder exceptions
follow_ups.why: _learn calls graphctx.ensure_fresh on the repo root and only catches AgentError, OSError, ValueError and KeyError, so a failing custom builder could surface unexpectedly there. Only list this if S3 does not cover it.

plan.goal: Record the ticket's repository identity, base SHA, and Graphify fingerprint/status as bounded trace metadata, and mark each graph.refresh span as either a real refresh or a no-op freshness check with node/edge counts. Missing or failed graphs must show up as explicit states and must never stop ticket execution.
out_of_scope: Changing how the graph fingerprint is computed or the freshness policy
Putting graph contents, digest text, file lists, prompts or error messages into metadata
Changes to Langfuse dashboards, setup scripts, the OTLP exporter, or the content-capture/redaction logic
Adding provenance to the CLI `graph status` output
Changing agent drivers or the digest/agent_preamble text
risks: The ticket.run span is created before the ticket is loaded. Base SHA and graph metadata can only be added once known, so spans emitted earlier in the same invocation (e.g. stage.new) will not carry them. The root span will, and the metadata is exported when the root span finishes.
Span attributes are inherited only at child creation. Trace-level graph metadata therefore reflects the latest check on the root span, and per-span truth lives on the graph.refresh span.
The fingerprint changes whenever the working tree changes. To keep cardinality low, record only a 12-char prefix and expose it per trace, never as a session id or a grouping key.
The remote URL may embed credentials. If the sanitizer cannot parse a URL cleanly, omit the remote rather than emit a partial value.

Changing the GraphStatus dataclass can break positional construction elsewhere. New fields must have defaults and be added at the end; the existing tests in tests/test_graphctx.py and cli.py usage must keep passing unchanged.

steps.description: Extend GraphStatus with `fingerprint: str = ''` and a derived `state` of fresh | refreshed | failed | unavailable. Map it as follows: no-op up-to-date -> fresh; successful rebuild -> refreshed; builder ran but not ok -> failed; builder did not run or there is no git repo -> unavailable. Populate the fingerprint in the no-op, rebuilt and failed branches. Leave the existing `refreshed`, `ok`, `nodes`, `edges` and `message` fields and their callers in cli.py and the existing tests untouched. Inside ensure_fresh, call a new telemetry helper to annotate the current graph.refresh span with devflow.graph.refreshed, .status, .nodes, .edges and .fingerprint (short hex). Do not put `message` in the attributes, because it can contain arbitrary stderr.

Add two telemetry helpers. `annotate(**attrs)` sets validated attributes on the current span. `trace_metadata(**values)` sets allowlisted provenance keys on the ticket.run root span as both langfuse.trace.metadata.<key> and devflow.<key>, so spans created afterwards inherit them. Track the root through a ContextVar set in ticket_run. Both helpers are no-ops when no span or root is active or telemetry is disabled, and never raise. Validation: hex regex for base_sha and fingerprint (fingerprint truncated to 12 chars), enum for graph status, non-negative ints for counts, and a sanitizer for the remote URL (drop userinfo, query and fragment; keep host/owner/repo). Drop any value that fails validation instead of writing it. Add the base_sha / graph keys to ticket_run's initial metadata only if available there; otherwise leave ticket_run as is.

In Engine.run, once the ticket is loaded, set trace metadata for base_sha from ticket.base_sha when present and the sanitized remote from cfg. In _new, set the base SHA right after worktree.create. Replace the bare `graphctx.ensure_fresh(wt, ...)` in _request with a small private helper that catches Exception, treats it as unavailable (no message recorded) and returns normally. The helper then calls telemetry.trace_metadata with the graph status, fingerprint and counts. Apply the same exception guard to the `_learn` call at ~line 713 only if it can be done without changing its error handling; otherwise list it as a follow-up.

Add tests in tests/test_graphctx.py. Use the existing Builder pattern to assert, via a capture log, the graph.refresh span attributes for fresh (builder not called, refreshed=false), refreshed (refreshed=true with counts), failed, and unavailable (GraphResult(False, False)). Also assert the fingerprint is truncated hex and that no message text leaks.

Add ticket-level tests in tests/test_telemetry.py using Env: (a) the default engine builder gives status=unavailable and the ticket.run attributes include base_sha equal to env.ticket().base_sha and the repo name; (b) an engine with a builder returning an ok GraphResult gives refreshed with counts on the trace; (c) a builder that raises still reaches the same final state as before and the trace shows unavailable; (d) a remote URL containing user:password@ is sanitized and the secret is absent from the log text; (e) the metadata keys appear with capture_content both off and on, and no prompt/issue text appears in them.

Document the new trace metadata keys, the graph.refresh attributes, the fresh / refreshed / failed / unavailable meanings, and the explicit exclusions (no graph contents, prompts or credentials) in the span table and the metadata section.
Run `ruff check .` and `python -m pytest`. Fix failures in the new code only; do not edit existing assertions to make them pass.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new test in tests/test_telemetry.py uses the Env fake host and fake agents with the default config (plan and merge gates on) and no network or provider calls. Invocation 1 ends in awaiting_plan_approval. After a plan /approve, invocation 2 ends in awaiting_merge_approval. After a PR /approve, invocation 3 ends in merged. The test asserts the review stage result says the reviewer was independent and approved before the merge-approval pause.

The log has exactly 3 'ticket.run' root spans (empty parent_id), each with a distinct trace_id. Every record has a trace_id belonging to one of these roots, and every non-root record's parent_id resolves to a span_id in the same trace_id. Walking parent_id from any record reaches that trace's ticket.run root.
All records carry the attribute langfuse.session.id equal to 't:issue-1', and each root has langfuse.trace.metadata.issue == '1'. The test asserts this for all three invocations.

Stage spans appear in the right invocation: stage.refining and stage.awaiting_plan_approval in the first and second; stage.test_design, stage.implementing, stage.gates, stage.in_review and stage.awaiting_merge_approval by the second; stage.awaiting_merge_approval again in the third. Each stage span's parent is its invocation's ticket.run span.

Agent spans exist with the expected names, parented under the matching stage span, with devflow.ok True and the expected devflow.role: agent.fake.planner under stage.refining, agent.claude.test_planner under stage.test_design, agent.claude.coder under stage.implementing, agent.codex.reviewer under stage.in_review. The planner span has devflow.resumed False.
At least one gate.result event is under stage.gates with devflow.gate 'unit' and devflow.ok True. Its trace_id equals that of the invocation containing the implementation stage.

state.transition records cover every transition in the ticket history (refining, awaiting_plan_approval, test_design, implementing, gates, in_review, awaiting_merge_approval, merged). Each is in the invocation where that transition happened and has devflow.state matching its target and a parent that is a stage span or the ticket.run span.

Pause spans have status 'waiting', not 'error'. The first invocation's ticket.run and its stage.awaiting_plan_approval span, and the second invocation's ticket.run and its stage.awaiting_merge_approval span, are all 'waiting'. The test asserts that no record in the whole lifecycle has status 'error'. The final ticket.run for the merged ticket is not waiting.

The test is deterministic and offline. It uses only Env, FakeHost, FakeAgent and the existing capture fixture. It reads no real clock-dependent values except for end_ns >= start_ns. It closes env.store in a finally block. Running 'python -m pytest' and 'ruff check .' pass, and the new test is collected by the existing unit gate with no gate command changes.

plan.goal: Extend the offline fake-agent telemetry test so it drives a ticket across three engine invocations, from issue through plan approval, implementation, gates, independent review and merge approval to the merge, and asserts trace parentage, session correlation, stage outcomes and the key agent, gate and state-transition records.
out_of_scope: Changing production telemetry, engine, gates or agent code. Only add test code, unless a real telemetry bug that the test exposes is the minimal fix, in which case record it as a follow-up instead of folding it in.
Adding a separate 'integration' gate, pytest marker or CI job. The repo configures only lint and unit (python -m pytest), and the new test is collected by that run.
Testing export to Langfuse or the OTLP HTTP path, or content capture and redaction. These are already covered by other tests.
Escalation, review-change-request or crash-recovery lifecycle paths. The ticket covers the approve-path lifecycle only.
Calls to real providers, GitHub or Docker.
risks: The ticket says 'configured integration gate', but the repo configures only lint and unit gates. The plan assumes the unit gate (python -m pytest) satisfies this. If a dedicated integration gate was intended, a human must say so.

Span and event names or parentage may differ from what the engine really emits (for example, a gate.result event may sit under tool.shell or stage.gates). Check the real shape in the log before asserting, and assert what the code produces, not what is assumed.
telemetry.configure sets global module state. The capture fixture resets it afterwards, so the test must use that fixture and not leave tracing enabled for later tests.

Tests depend on the Env fixture in tests/test_engine.py, which creates git repos and a local bare origin. The test stays offline but touches the filesystem and git. Keep it independent of the developer's real git config, as the other Env tests are.
Records are appended per run to one JSONL file. Group them by trace_id, not by file order, so interleaving or flush timing cannot break the assertions.

steps.description: Read the existing test_full_ticket_emits_stage_agent_gate_and_state_spans and test_full_ticket_from_issue_to_merge. Reuse the Env pattern (env.engine().run(1), env.say('alice','/approve'), env.say('alice','/approve', number=env.pr())). Confirm the span names and attributes asserted below against src/devflow/telemetry.py (span, ticket_run, agent_call), src/devflow/engine.py (run, _move) and src/devflow/gates.py (gate.result). Do not change them.

Add small helpers in tests/test_telemetry.py. One splits rows(capture) into per-invocation groups keyed by the ticket.run root's trace_id and returns roots in start_ns order. One returns the ancestor chain via a span_id index. One finds records by name within a trace. Keep helpers private to the test module.

Add the new test, e.g. test_full_lifecycle_trace_spans_three_invocations_and_one_session. It uses the capture fixture and Env(tmp_path / 'ticket'). Run invocation 1, then say plan /approve and run invocation 2 (to merge approval), then say PR /approve and run invocation 3 (to merged). Assert the ticket states after each run. Wrap the body in try/finally that closes env.store. Leave the existing test_full_ticket_emits_stage_agent_gate_and_state_spans untouched.

In the new test, assert AC2 and AC3: exactly 3 roots with distinct trace_ids, every parent_id resolves within its own trace, all records carry session id 't:issue-1', and the roots carry issue metadata. Then assert AC4 to AC7: stage spans, agent spans with role, name and ok, gate.result for unit with ok True, and one state.transition per history entry matching env.ticket().history. Assert each in the correct invocation and under the expected parent.

Assert AC8: waiting statuses on the first and second invocations' roots and the stage spans that raised the pause, no record with status 'error' anywhere, and the third root not waiting. Also assert the review stage result is independent and approved before the second invocation ends.

Run 'ruff check .' and 'python -m pytest' (the configured lint and unit gates). Run the new test several times to check for flakiness. Do not add pytest markers, new gates or config changes: the full suite is what the repo's configured gates run.

review.reason:
The plan has two defects a coding agent could not resolve without guessing. Revise both and resubmit.

1. The integration gate is invented. Plan step 6, the goal text, AC7 and the risks all treat `python -m pytest tests/test_engine.py tests/test_telemetry.py` as the repo's 'configured integration gate'. No such gate exists. The root project's gates are only lint (`ruff check .`) and unit (`python -m pytest`). `.devflow/config.toml` is not in the checkout, and `git ls-files .devflow` returns nothing. Nothing in pyproject, CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `python -m pytest -q`), CONTRIBUTING.md or the docs defines that command. Step 6 then tells the coder to create the missing config file, or else add a note to CONTRIBUTING.md if it 'cannot be committed'. That fallback leaves the outcome open and puts config outside the ticket's scope.
   - Pick one explicit path. The simplest is to put the test in tests/test_telemetry.py, where the full-suite unit gate `python -m pytest` already runs it, and note that no separate integration gate is configured in the repo. Alternatively, state exactly which tracked file will define the integration gate and what it will contain.
   - Remove the claim that the command is already configured.
   - Do not make AC7 depend on an untracked file.

2. AC4 contradicts the Env fixture. In tests/test_engine.py, `Env.engine()` builds `FakeAgent(..., name='claude')` for the coder and `name='codex'` for the reviewer. The test planner role also runs on the 'claude' agent. The span names are therefore `agent.fake.planner`, `agent.claude.coder`, `agent.claude.test_planner` and `agent.codex.reviewer`. The plan's `agent.fake.*` for planner, coder and reviewer is wrong for two of the three.
   - The real history is refining, awaiting_plan_approval, test_design, implementing, gates, in_review, awaiting_merge_approval, then merged. See `test_full_ticket_from_issue_to_merge`. AC4's 'full chain' omits test_design, and `stage.test_design` is also missing. An exact-chain assertion written to the plan would fail.
   - Rewrite AC4 with the real span names and the real transition list, including test_design. Say whether the chain is asserted exactly or as an ordered subsequence.

3. Remove the invocation-3 hedge. Step 3 says 'MERGED if the FakeHost merge path supports it, otherwise the next stored state', and the risks section repeats the hedge. The existing tests show FakeHost does merge: `/approve` on `env.pr()` then `run(1)` gives `State.MERGED` and `env.host.merged == [env.pr()]`. Specify that invocation 3 uses `env.say('alice', '/approve', number=env.pr())` (the PR number, not issue 1) and asserts MERGED. The plan's 'second /approve' omits this, and a coder who approves on issue 1 would not resume the merge gate.
   - Decide whether the merged-stage spans are also asserted, since the ticket mentions the 'subsequent resume'.

The overall direction is sound: keep the test in tests/test_telemetry.py, use the `capture` fixture, check trace and session correlation, and do not count waiting spans as failures.

acceptance_criteria.text: The new or extended test lives in tests/test_telemetry.py, which the integration gate (`python -m pytest tests/test_engine.py tests/test_telemetry.py`, from the `integration` entry under `[project.gates]` in the loaded .devflow/config.toml) already collects. Running that exact command executes the test and it passes. The test is not unit-only and does not rely on a gate or marker that is not in that command.

The test drives at least three separate `Engine.run(1)` invocations with fresh engines: (1) refine, then pause at awaiting_plan_approval; (2) after alice's `/approve`, test_design, implementing, gates and in_review, then pause at awaiting_merge_approval; (3) after alice's `/approve` on the PR, merge to MERGED. It asserts the ticket state reached after each invocation. It asserts the review stage result is approved and independent (reviewer agent differs from coder agent), and that the merge-approval pause is reached only after implementing, gates and in_review have run.

Every `ticket.run` record, one per invocation, carries `langfuse.session.id == "t:issue-1"`. Each invocation has a distinct, non-empty `trace_id`, so the number of distinct trace IDs equals the number of invocations. Every non-root record in an invocation carries that invocation's `trace_id` and the session ID.

Parent/trace consistency holds for every record. Each non-root record's `parent_id` resolves to a `span_id` that exists in the same trace. Each `stage.<state>` span is a direct child of that invocation's `ticket.run`. `agent.*` spans, `gate.result` events, `state.transition` events and `tool.git` records are descendants of a stage span or of `ticket.run` in the same trace. Each `ticket.run` has no parent.

Required observations are present. Stage spans exist for refining, awaiting_plan_approval, test_design, implementing, gates, in_review and awaiting_merge_approval. Agent spans exist for the planner, coder, and reviewer roles. At least one `gate.result` event carries `devflow.gate` and `devflow.ok == True`. `state.transition` events cover the transition sequence refining, awaiting_plan_approval, test_design, implementing, gates, in_review, awaiting_merge_approval, merged. Each is present in the invocation in which it happened.

Pause and waiting outcomes are not failures. The `ticket.run` records for invocations 1 and 2 have status `waiting`, as does the stage span that raised the wait. No record in the happy-path lifecycle has status `error`. The final invocation's `ticket.run` is not `waiting` or `error`.

The test is deterministic and offline: it uses only FakeAgent, FakeHost, RecordingNotifier and the local bare-git origin from the existing `Env` fixture, with no network, real provider CLI, GitHub call or sleep. Telemetry goes to the `capture` fixture's local JSONL log with no collector endpoint configured. Assertions do not depend on timing, span ordering across runs, or random IDs beyond equality and distinctness.
`ruff check .` and `python -m pytest` still pass, and the existing telemetry tests, including the current plan-pause-and-resume test, still pass unchanged or are strictly strengthened.

acceptance_criteria.text: A reusable validator (e.g. `devflow.telemetry.check_trace_completeness(rows)`, or a new `devflow/tracecheck.py`) takes exported span records and returns a list of structured violations, empty when the trace is complete. It checks that each invocation slice has exactly one `ticket.run` root with empty parent_id and a single shared trace_id. Every span reaches its root through parent_ids that exist within the same slice, with no orphans, dangling parents or cycles. All records carry the same `langfuse.session.id`.

Across the three-invocation lifecycle (new→awaiting_plan_approval, then →awaiting_merge_approval, then →merged), the validator requires a `stage.*` span for each required stage: plan (`stage.refining`), test_plan (`stage.test_design`), implement (`stage.implementing`), gates (`stage.gates`) and review (`stage.in_review`). Each of these must be a direct child of the `ticket.run` root of its invocation and its `devflow.state` attribute must match its name. If any required stage span is absent, or present but with a missing or unknown parent, the validator reports it.

The validator also requires that the required child spans stay attached to the right stage: `agent.*` spans under their owning stage, and `gate.result` and `state.transition` spans under a `stage.*` span. Any that sit under a non-stage parent or are missing are reported.

A test in `tests/test_telemetry.py` (so it runs in the configured integration gate `python -m pytest tests/test_engine.py tests/test_telemetry.py` and in the unit gate) runs the real `Env` three-invocation lifecycle with the file exporter and asserts the validator returns no violations. The test uses only local tmp files and fake agents/host, with no network or Langfuse dependency, and is deterministic across repeated runs.

Negative tests mutate a captured trace (drop `stage.test_design`, drop each other required stage, re-parent a stage to a nonexistent id, re-parent a stage to a non-root span, change one record's session id, delete the root) and assert the validator flags each case. Each case is flagged with a distinct, specific violation, not just a generic failure.

Diagnostics are clear. Each violation message names the check that failed, the invocation slice, and the offending span name and span_id (or the missing stage name), for example `slice 2: required stage span 'stage.gates' (gates) missing` or `slice 1: span 'stage.implementing' (id=ab12) parent 'zz99' not found`. The gating test fails with the joined violation list in the assertion message, and a test asserts the message text of at least two violation kinds.

`ruff check .` and `python -m pytest` pass. The existing `test_full_lifecycle_traces_span_three_invocations_with_consistent_parentage` and other existing assertions are not weakened or deleted. They may be refactored only to share the capture fixture or helper.

CI continues to enforce the check, and the CI workflow and docs reflect it. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs the full pytest suite, which includes the new gate, so a regression turns the `test` job red. If a separate named step is added, it runs only `python -m pytest tests/test_telemetry.py -k trace_completeness` without extra network setup. `docs/observability.md` gets a short paragraph on the trace-completeness gate: what it checks and how to run it locally.

The lifecycle is split across three engine invocations, each with its own trace_id. A validator that demanded all five stages inside one trace would always fail. It must check required stages across the ticket's slices and parentage within each slice.

acceptance_criteria.text: A pure function computes p50/p90/p99 over a list of durations using linear interpolation between closest ranks. A single sample returns that sample for every percentile. An empty list is handled without raising. Results are rounded to 3 decimals. Unit tests pin exact values for 1, 2, 5 and 100 samples.

`devflow telemetry metrics` (aggregate mode) gives each `stage_latency_seconds[stage.*]` entry `count`, `mean`, `max`, `p50`, `p90` and `p99`. Output stays valid strict JSON. Synthetic spans and `stage.result` stay excluded, and non-finite or malformed timestamps stay ignored, as they are today.

`devflow telemetry metrics --issue N` gives the per-session and top-level `stage_latency_seconds` entries the same percentile keys. Agent latency entries (`agent_latency_seconds`) are unchanged: `count`, `mean`, `max` only.

A pure stall detector takes the stage name, the elapsed seconds and prior stage durations. It reports a stall only when at least 5 prior samples exist and elapsed seconds exceed that stage's p99. It reports no stall and does not raise for fewer than 5 samples, an empty history, or elapsed exactly equal to p99. Baseline durations come only from non-synthetic `stage.*` spans with status `ok`, so `waiting` (human pause) and `error` spans do not skew the baseline. Unit tests cover each of these cases.

During a real engine run, after each stage finishes, the engine checks the stage's duration against the baseline read from the local telemetry log. On a stall it emits a telemetry event named `stall.detected`. The name must not start with `stage.`, or the metrics aggregation would count it as a stage latency. The event carries `devflow.stage`, `devflow.duration_seconds`, `devflow.threshold_p99_seconds` and `devflow.baseline_samples`. It also prints one `devflow: stall warning: ...` line to stderr. A normal-speed stage emits neither.

With telemetry disabled or no log file configured, the stall check is a no-op. An unreadable or malformed log never raises, never stops or changes ticket state transitions, and never adds model calls. Stage timeout behaviour (`stage_timeout_minutes`) is unchanged.
`telemetry metrics` reports a `stage_stalls` mapping of stage name to count of `stall.detected` events (empty `{}` when none), without including attribute values beyond stage names and counts.

Existing assertions that compare stage stats by exact equality in tests/test_telemetry_metrics.py are updated for the new keys. Agent-stat assertions are unchanged. No test is weakened, skipped or deleted.

Integration tests in tests/test_engine.py and/or tests/test_telemetry.py run a real Engine with telemetry pointed at a temp JSONL log. Seed history of at least 5 fast `stage.*` spans, then slow a stage handler past the seeded p99: the `stall.detected` event is written to the log and the stderr warning appears. A control run with a fast stage produces no stall.

`docs/observability.md` documents the percentile fields, the `stall.detected` event, and the detection rule (p99, minimum 5 samples, ok-status spans only, post-completion check). `README.md`'s metrics section is updated if it lists the metrics fields. `ruff check .`, `python -m pytest` and `python -m pytest tests/test_engine.py tests/test_telemetry.py` all pass.

acceptance_criteria.text: graphctx exposes a read-only check, e.g. `graph_freshness(root) -> str`, that returns exactly one of `fresh`, `stale`, `unbuilt` and writes nothing. `unbuilt`: `graphify-out/graph.json` is missing. `fresh`: graph.json exists and the stored `.devflow_fingerprint` equals the current `fingerprint(root)`. `stale`: graph.json exists but the stored fingerprint is missing or differs (HEAD moved or the working tree changed). A non-git directory or a git error returns `unbuilt` or `stale`, never raises.

When the planner request is built (the REFINING stage, role `planner`), the freshness check runs BEFORE `_refresh_graph` rebuilds the graph, so a graph that is stale at plan time is reported even though the engine then auto-rebuilds it. Other roles (reviewer, coder, etc.) do not emit the warning.

For `stale` or `unbuilt` the engine emits one `graph.stale` trace event (only allowlisted attributes: `devflow.graph.status` set to stale/unbuilt, `devflow.graph.fingerprint` (12-char prefix, via `_valid`), `devflow.graph.stored_fingerprint` (12-char prefix, or empty), `devflow.graph.age_seconds` (int, omitted if unbuilt)). It also prints one stderr line starting `devflow: graph warning:` that names the state and says the planner may see obsolete or missing symbols. `fresh` emits no event and no warning.

The warning outcome is attached to the trace root as allowlisted metadata, e.g. a new `graph_staleness` key (values `fresh|stale|unbuilt`, validated in `telemetry._valid`/`_TRACE_KEYS`, mirrored as `devflow.graph_staleness` and `langfuse.trace.metadata.graph_staleness`). Invalid values are dropped. The existing `graph_status` metadata and the `graph.refresh` span keep their current values and semantics.

The check can never stop or fail a ticket: any exception inside it, or inside telemetry/printing, is swallowed (best effort), and the existing request flow, including `graph_builder` failures, behaves as before. The post-check state (rebuilt, failed or unavailable) still comes from `_refresh_graph`. If the rebuild fails or is unavailable after a stale/unbuilt result, the warning is still emitted.

Tests cover all three states at both levels. In tests/test_graphctx.py, `graph_freshness` returns `unbuilt` with no graph, `fresh` after `ensure_fresh` builds it, and `stale` after a new commit and after an uncommitted edit; it makes no writes, and a git error does not raise. In tests/test_engine.py and/or tests/test_telemetry.py, a planner request on a fresh graph emits no `graph.stale` event and no stderr warning. On a stale graph it emits exactly one event, one stderr line and `graph_staleness=stale` on the root span. On an unbuilt graph, with the builder both succeeding and failing, it emits the event and `graph_staleness=unbuilt`. A non-planner role emits none. The warning attributes contain no free text and no file paths.

docs/observability.md lists the `graph.stale` event in the span table and `graph_staleness` in the provenance metadata section, with the stale/unbuilt/fresh definitions. All three configured gates pass: `ruff check .`, `python -m pytest`, `python -m pytest tests/test_engine.py tests/test_telemetry.py`.

plan.goal: At the start of the planner stage, check the Graphify code graph against the ticket worktree before it is refreshed, and when it is stale or unbuilt, log a clear warning and record it on the ticket's trace, without ever blocking the ticket.
out_of_scope: Changing the auto-refresh behaviour: the engine still rebuilds a stale graph and does not block planning on staleness.
A configurable age or time-based staleness threshold, or any new config setting.
Warnings at non-planner stages (reviewer, coder, retro) or in the CLI/UI beyond the stderr line.
Changing the `graph.refresh` span, the `GraphStatus` states, or the existing `graph_status` trace metadata.
Posting the warning to the GitHub issue or sending a notifier message.
risks: Because the engine rebuilds the graph right after the check, `stale` will normally be followed by `refreshed`; the warning therefore means "stale when planning began", not "the planner saw a stale graph". The message and docs must say so, and the case that matters most is a stale graph whose rebuild failed (status `failed` or `unavailable`).

In a fresh ticket worktree the graph is often missing or built for another commit, so the warning could fire on nearly every ticket. That is accepted noise for now, and the event is a single trace event and one stderr line rather than an issue comment.

`fingerprint()` runs several git subprocesses and hashes untracked files, and `ensure_fresh` computes it again right after. The double cost is small but real; it could be avoided by passing the computed fingerprint through if it shows up in the stage latency baselines.
Adding a trace-metadata key touches the telemetry allowlist, and existing tests assert the exact allowed key set; those assertions must be updated deliberately rather than loosened.

acceptance_criteria.text: `graphctx.symbols_for_files(root, files)` reads graphify-out/graph.json and returns a deterministically sorted list of symbol records (id, label, file, line parsed from source_location, role). Role `defined` means a code node whose source_file is one of the given files. File-level container nodes, rationale/concept nodes and nodes without a source_file are excluded. Role `touched` means a code symbol in another file that is the target of an edge whose own source_file is a given file, which covers callees, referenced classes and imported names. Input paths are normalised to repo-relative posix paths, and absolute paths under root are accepted. Files with no nodes in the graph are returned in an `unknown_files` list instead of raising.

`graphctx.blast_radius(root, files, depth=2)` runs a reverse breadth-first search from the `defined` symbols along inbound `calls`, `indirect_call`, `uses`, `references`, `inherits` and `method` edges. It returns callers grouped by hop (1..depth), each with symbol, file, hop number and the relation that connected it. A symbol appears only at its shortest hop and never at hop 0. depth=1 returns only direct callers, depth=2 adds callers of callers, and depth<1 raises ValueError.

The blast_radius result also contains `dependent_modules`: the sorted unique files, excluding the modified files, that import a modified file (via `imports` or `imports_from` edges) or contain a caller found in AC2. Each entry carries its minimum hop. Modules that import a modified file appear at hop 1, even when no symbol-level edge exists.

The blast_radius result contains `external_contracts`. These are the public (no leading underscore) symbols defined in the modified files that have at least one inbound edge from a symbol in a different file, plus symbols re-exported through a `re_exports` edge. Each entry lists its consumer files. A private symbol or a symbol used only inside its own file is not a contract.

`graphctx.test_coverage_map(root, symbols)` returns a mapping from each given symbol id to a sorted list of test files that exercise it. A test file is a file under `tests/` or `test/`, or one named `test_*.py` or `*_test.py`. A test file exercises a symbol when some node in it reaches the symbol through at most 2 hops of the AC2 edge types, or when the test file itself is among the modified files. Symbols with no covering test map to an empty list, and the report lists them under `uncovered`.

An `impact(root, files, depth=2)` function composes AC1-AC5 into an ImpactReport dataclass. acceptance_criteria.text: A new pure function in src/devflow/graphctx.py renders a bounded, deterministic 'blast radius and contract verification checklist' from an ImpactReport and the changed-file list. When the report is empty it says so. Output is capped at a fixed character budget with a truncation marker. Labels and paths are passed through the existing `_clean` helper so graph text cannot inject instructions.

`prompts.reviewer_task` accepts an optional keyword `blast_radius: str | None = None`. When it is non-empty the prompt contains a fenced `BLAST RADIUS` block and one sentence telling the reviewer to treat it as graph-derived data and to tick or reject each checklist item, with a blocking finding for any caller contract that is broken. When it is None or empty the prompt is byte-identical to today's.

In `Engine._in_review`, the blast radius is computed with `graphctx.impact(review_wt, gitops.diff_names(review_wt, t.base_sha))` after the review worktree exists and before the reviewer request is built. The resulting checklist reaches the reviewer prompt. If the graph is missing or unreadable, or impact raises, review proceeds without the block and the trace records `blast_status=unavailable`. A graph failure never stops or fails a ticket.

`gates.run_gates` accepts an optional `impacted_tests: list[str]` (test file paths relative to the repo root) and an optional `priority_check` callback. For each configured command that is a recognisable pytest invocation (`pytest ...` or `python -m pytest ...` with no explicit path arguments), it first runs that command with the existing impacted test files appended, as a priority pass. If `priority_check(result)` returns True for a failed priority result, the wider suite for that command is skipped, and the priority result is recorded in `report.results` under the ORIGINAL command string so baseline keys still match. Otherwise the full original command still runs and its result is the one recorded in `report.results`. The priority result is kept in a separate `report.priority` list for diagnostics only. Commands that are not recognisable pytest invocations, and runs with no impacted tests, behave exactly as today. Impacted paths that do not exist in the worktree are dropped.

`Engine._verify` computes the impacted test files from the same ImpactReport (the union of `test_coverage` values and any modified test files in the diff). It passes them to `run_gates` with a `priority_check` that uses `baseline.evaluate`: a priority failure short-circuits only when it has failure fingerprints that are new compared with the base report. Pre-existing failures never short-circuit and never become new blockers. `_gates` and `_in_review` verdicts are otherwise unchanged. When the graph is unavailable, gates run exactly as before.

Trace metadata on the ticket root gets validated, allowlisted keys: `blast_status` ('injected' or 'unavailable'), `blast_nodes`, `blast_edges`, `blast_callers_total`, `blast_callers_verified`, `impacted_tests`. `telemetry._valid` and `_TRACE_KEYS` are extended with the validation kinds these need. A caller is 'verified' when its file is in the diff or is a test file, and 'unverified' otherwise. A `gate.order` event records `impacted_tests`, `priority_ran`, `priority_ok` and `short_circuited`, with no file contents or prompt text.

Unit tests in tests/test_graphctx.py cover the checklist: items for contracts, outside-diff callers and uncovered symbols; determinism; the budget and truncation marker; an empty report; and sanitised hostile labels. Tests in tests/test_gates.py cover the priority pass: the impacted tests run before the wider command; a passing priority pass still runs the full command; a short-circuit records the original command; non-pytest commands are unchanged; missing paths are dropped.

Integration tests in tests/test_engine.py use the seeded graph builder pattern already there. They assert that (a) the reviewer request's prompt contains the BLAST RADIUS block with the expected contract, caller and uncovered-symbol lines, and the coder and planner prompts do not; (b) `_verify`/gate execution runs the impacted test file first, as seen in the order of commands run; (c) a graph failure at review time still completes review with no block and `blast_status=unavailable`; (d) a priority failure that already exists on the base does not short-circuit. follow_ups.title: Surface gate output tails and diff stat in the inspector on demand
follow_ups.why: Output tails are capped for payload size, so a full failing-test log needs a separate bounded, opt-in endpoint.

follow_ups.title: UI server has no auth or CSRF/host-header protection beyond binding to 127.0.0.1

plan.goal: Make the `devflow ui` board interactive: clicking a ticket opens a deep-linkable slide-over inspector drawer (Overview, Plan, Blast radius, Gates tabs) fed by a new `GET /api/ticket/<issue>` endpoint that aggregates SQLite ticket and stage data, the persisted gate and impact evidence, and matching trace spans.
out_of_scope: Any write actions from the UI (approve, resume, retry, edit plan); the drawer is read-only.
A new markdown, JS or CSS framework or bundler, or any external network asset.
Backfilling gate or impact evidence for tickets already merged before this change. Legacy tickets show empty sections.
Changing the board columns, the polling interval, or the `/api/state` contract beyond additive fields.
A runs table redesign; any existing runs table only gets the same click handler.
Running `graphify` or `devflow graph impact` live from the UI server; only persisted impact data is shown.
Changing how Langfuse/OTLP export or telemetry redaction works.
risks: Contract: the `gates` stage payload shape is consumed by `Engine._gates`, `_latest(t, 'gates')`, `test_engine.py` (lines ~317/367/394/420) and `tests/test_telemetry.py` through `telemetry.content_event('stage.result')`. New keys must be purely additive; the telemetry content event will now carry larger payloads, so output_tail and impact size must be capped to stay within `max_content_characters` and redaction.

Contract: `Engine._verify` and `Engine._impact` are used from both `_gates` and `_review`, and `Env`/`Engine` in tests/test_engine.py is the most connected symbol in the graph (138 links). Changing the `_verify` return or call signature would ripple through many tests, so keep the signature and read the report via the existing third return value.
Contract: `ImpactReport.to_dict()` (graphctx) is the public schema for impact data, tested in tests/test_graphctx.py. The UI must read it as-is and tolerate missing keys; do not change that schema.

`Ticket.issue` can be None for local-only tickets and `collect_state` keys on it. The new lookup must not crash on None, and the issue-to-ticket mapping must not collide when a ticket id is `#<n>` versus `<n>`.

XSS: issue bodies, review summaries and file paths come from external people and tools, and the existing template builds HTML via `innerHTML` and interpolates `item.stage` and `item.priority` unescaped. The drawer must escape everything and restrict link schemes. Consider also escaping those existing fields.

The 3s poll currently clears `board-container.innerHTML` and rebuilds cards, which would drop focus and click handlers and could close or rebuild an open drawer. Use event delegation on the container and keep the drawer outside the polled subtree, as AC10 requires.

`GhHost.get_issue` shells out to `gh` and can hang or need auth. Use a short timeout, never call it while holding the Store connection, and avoid per-poll calls. A ThreadingMixIn server means slow calls only block their own request.

The traces log can be large; read it line by line, tolerate malformed JSON, and never return attribute values (they may hold captured content). Only names, durations and outcomes go out, matching `issue_metrics` conventions.

The Store opens a SQLite connection per request. Read-only access must not create `.devflow/state` or an empty DB as a side effect on a repo with no devflow state (note `Store.__init__` does mkdir); check `db.exists()` first as `collect_state` does.
The existing e2e test uses the real repo root and an optional Chrome binary; new tests must use `tmp_path` and not depend on Chrome so the unit gate stays deterministic.

steps.description: Persist the evidence the drawer needs. In `Engine._gates`, keep the `GateReport` that `_verify` currently discards and compute the impact once. Add to the `gates` stage payload `results` (per-command: project, gate, command, ok, exit_code, duration_s, timed_out, output_tail capped at ~2KB), `failures` (from `verdict.new_failures`: project, gate, command, new[:20]), `impact` (`impact.to_dict()` or None) and `impacted_tests`. Keep existing keys intact. In `_review`, also store a bounded `impact` and `gate_results` in the `review` payload (or reference the latest gates payload) so reviewed-commit evidence is available after approval. Reuse `Engine._blast_radius`/`graphctx.impacted_tests` for the test ordering rather than recomputing differently. Wrap the impact serialization so it can never raise and stop a ticket.

Add `collect_ticket(root, issue, *, host_factory=None) -> dict | None` in `ui.py`. Read the ticket by issue from `Store` (match `Ticket.issue`; tickets table id is a string like `#38`). Pull the latest `plan`, `test_plan`, `gates` (all attempts), `review` and `implement` stage results, plus the `transition` history. Derive `lifecycle` from `State` (refining/awaiting_* → Refining, implementing/test_design/changes_requested → Implementing, gates → Gates, in_review/awaiting_merge_approval → Review, merged → Merged, escalated/cancelled → Failed) and the coding agent from the `implement` payload or `sessions['coder_agent']`. Build the PR URL from `sessions['pr']` and the repo slug already computed in `collect_state`. Strip `reply` and other large free-text fields. Build `blast_radius` from the persisted impact: symbols, hop-1 callers with verified flag (from the existing Caller dict), dependent_modules, uncovered, impacted_tests. Read `traces.jsonl` defensively, reusing `telemetry_cli._matches_issue`/`_is_synthetic` (or a small shared helper) and returning name, duration and outcome only. Fetch the issue body through a best-effort host call wrapped in try/except with a short timeout. Return None for unknown tickets.

Route `GET /api/ticket/<id>` in `UiHandler.do_GET`: parse the path with `urllib.parse` (ignore the query string), validate that the id is a positive integer (400), return 404 JSON for unknown tickets, and return 500 JSON only for unexpected errors. Mirror the existing `/api/state` headers (`Content-Type`, `Content-Length`, `Cache-Control: no-cache`). Keep `/`, `/api/state` and the 404 fallthrough behaving as before, and have `/` ignore a hash, which is client-side only. Make the handler's host factory overridable (class attribute) so tests can inject a fake.

Extend `collect_state` so each card carries what the drawer needs without extra round trips. Include `issue`, `lifecycle` and `stage`, and make sure local-only tickets still list when `item.issue` is None-safe. Do not change existing keys.

Implement the drawer UI in `HTML_TEMPLATE` (vanilla CSS and JS). Add the drawer and overlay markup, the slide transition, the carbon palette variables scoped to the drawer, the tab bar, and the per-tab renderers. Overview has the markdown brief, metadata chips and GitHub issue/PR links. Plan has objectives, files, criteria, test strategy and a collapsible `<details>` reasoning excerpt. Blast radius has the symbols, hop-1 callers with verified/unverified badges, dependent modules, uncovered symbols and the test ordering summary. Gates has command rows with pass/fail badge, exit code and duration, failure fingerprints, and reviewer findings, checklist and approval. Add a small allow-list markdown-to-HTML function that escapes first, and a safe-link helper that accepts only http(s). Wire card click and Enter/Space, ESC, backdrop click and a close button. Wire the hash handling (`#ticket-<n>`, `hashchange`, initial open after the first fetch), and focus management and ARIA roles. Guard the poll re-render so the open drawer is not rebuilt, and avoid refetching the ticket on every poll tick beyond a lightweight refresh of the active ticket.

Write the tests. In `tests/test_ui.py`, seed a `Store` in `tmp_path/.devflow/state/devflow.db` and test `collect_ticket` plus the live server endpoint (ephemeral-port pattern already used there) for all AC1–AC8 cases. Add template-marker assertions for AC9–AC12 and keep the existing tests green. In `tests/test_engine.py`, extend an existing gates test to assert `results`, `failures` and `impact` are persisted. Do not weaken or delete existing tests.

Docs and verification. Add a short note on the inspector drawer and the `/api/ticket/<id>` shape to the README or docs (existing `devflow ui` mention), then run the gates in order: `ruff check .`, `python -m pytest`, and `python -m pytest tests/test_engine.py tests/test_telemetry.py`. If Chrome is present, take a headless screenshot of `/#ticket-<n>` against a seeded repo as a smoke check; the existing browser test skips without Chrome.

review.reason: The plan is executable as written. I checked the symbols it names against the repo, and they exist where it says: telemetry_cli._matches_issue, stall._is_synthetic, host.get_issue, and Engine._impact, _verify (returning verdict, findings and a GateReport), _gates and _review. It correctly sees that _gates currently discards the GateReport and persists only ok, summary, unconfigured and findings. It adds the missing evidence additively (results, failures, impact) without changing the _verify signature. All 14 acceptance criteria are concrete and testable. They cover the API shape and the 400/404 cases, the legacy payload, malformed traces, the host-failure fallback, XSS safety, ESC/backdrop/hash behaviour, and poll survival. Tests are planned in tests/test_ui.py and tests/test_engine.py. The configured integration gate (python -m pytest tests/test_engine.py tests/test_telemetry.py) is in AC14 and S7 alongside ruff and the unit pytest run. The plan also handles the real risks: Ticket.issue can be None, the Store constructor creates directories so db.exists() must be checked first, the poll re-render must not rebuild the drawer, payload sizes are capped for telemetry content events, and out-of-scope items are explicit. Minor notes for the coder, none of them blocking: S4 is thin, so keep its changes strictly additive. In the review step, prefer a bounded reference or summary over duplicating large payloads. Make sure the host call's timeout works for hosts that have none, for example by running it in a worker thread with a deadline.

acceptance_criteria.text: A pure function `uilane.touches_ui(changed_files, patterns)` in the new `src/devflow/uilane.py` returns the matching files. Its default patterns match `src/devflow/ui.py`, `site/**`, `**/static/**`, and `*.html|*.css|*.js|*.jsx|*.ts|*.tsx|*.vue|*.svelte` files. It does not match backend-only changes such as `src/devflow/engine.py`, `tests/test_gates.py`, or prompt templates like `src/devflow/templates/*.md`. A `[ui] paths` list in config.toml overrides the defaults, and invalid values raise `ConfigError`. Unit tests cover all of these cases.

When `[ui]` is configured and the diff since `base_sha` touches UI files, `Engine._verify` runs the UI lane in addition to `run_gates`, and the result is attached to the returned `GateReport` through a new optional `ui` field. When the diff touches only backend files, or `[ui]` is absent, the UI lane is not run and the gate report, stage payloads and fake-agent call counts are identical to today. Tests assert both branches, including that the lane command is not invoked for a backend-only diff.

The plan schema gains an optional `ui_use_cases` array of objects with `id`, `title`, `kind` (happy_path | state_persistence | error_state | responsive | deep_link | other), `description` and `criterion_ids`. After planning, the engine checks the plan: if any step file matches the UI patterns and `[ui]` is enabled, the plan must contain 3–6 well-formed use cases whose `criterion_ids` exist, and each use case needs a non-empty id and description. A violating plan is not accepted and returns to REFINING via `plan_feedback`, using the same re-plan mechanism as the test-design traceability failure. Non-UI plans are not required to have use cases. Tests cover accept, too few, too many, unknown criterion, and non-UI plans.

The deterministic runner lets a Playwright-based pytest suite exercise the live app. The lane command is `[ui] command`, run in the ticket worktree with a scrubbed environment plus `DEVFLOW_UI_REPORT`, `DEVFLOW_UI_ARTIFACTS` and `DEVFLOW_UI_PORT`. No agent is called while it runs. The repo ships `tests/ui/` scenarios for `devflow ui` (served on an ephemeral port via a fixture) that each declare the use-case ids they cover. A scenario's use-case ids come from a `ui_case` marker or helper, and the case records the ids.

The runner captures `console` messages of type warning/error, uncaught `pageerror` events, failed requests, and responses with status >= 400. Any captured item fails that case, and therefore the lane and the gate, even if the test's own assertions passed. The failure message names the offending item (type and text, or URL and status). Unit tests drive a fake page object with `.on(event, handler)` to prove each of the four capture paths fails the case without needing Playwright. A Playwright integration test, skipped when Playwright or its browsers are unavailable, injects a real console error, a pageerror and a 500 and asserts they are caught.

The lane writes a JSON report `{cases:[{id,use_case_ids,ok,duration_s,errors,console,page_errors,network_failures,screenshot,dom}]}`. The engine parses it with `uilane.load_report`, which is strict about shape. The lane fails if the command exits non-zero, times out, writes no report or an invalid one, any case fails, or any plan use-case id is covered by no case. Each failure reason is explicit in the failure text fed back to the coder. A missing browser or Playwright makes the lane fail loudly ('UI lane unavailable: ...') and never passes silently. Unit tests cover each outcome with a stub command writing fixture reports.

If the diff touches UI files but no `[ui] command` is configured, the lane is recorded as unconfigured (an entry like `ui:browser lane` in `verdict.unconfigured` and in the gate evidence), consistent with how missing gates are reported. It does not fail the ticket. UI lane failures are strict and not compared to the baseline, since console errors on the base would be noise. They add a `NewFailure(project='.', gate='ui', ...)`, so `Verdict.ok` becomes False and `_gates` routes the ticket back to IMPLEMENTING. `_failure_text` includes the failing case ids and captured errors. Tests assert this routing.

A new `ui_evaluator` role has a prompt template `templates/ui_evaluator.md` and a schema `schemas/ui_evaluation.schema.json`: `{use_cases:[{id,status:pass|fail|missing,case_ids,evidence}], findings:[{id,severity,blocking,summary}], notes}`. During IN_REVIEW, after the deterministic lane has run and passed, the engine calls it once with the plan's use-case matrix, the acceptance criteria and a bounded digest of the lane report (case results, error summaries, artifact paths). The evaluator is not given a browser and is not asked to drive anything. It runs through the same agent selection as the reviewer, avoiding the coder's agent where possible. It is not called when the lane did not run, failed deterministically, or was unconfigured. Tests with fake agents assert the call count and that the prompt carries the matrix and report digest.

The evaluator verdict cannot override the engine. A `fail` or `missing` use case, or a blocking evaluator finding, becomes a blocking review finding and blocks approval. An evaluator that returns `pass` for a use case with no passing case in the deterministic report is corrected by the engine to `missing`. Tests cover each branch.

The combined gate report carries a 'Feature Use-Case Verification' markdown table (use case id, title, kind, mapped case ids, status, evidence). It appears in (a) the `gates` and `review` stage payloads under a new additive `ui_lane` / `ui_verification` key, (b) the PR review comment built by `_format_review`, and (c) the reviewer prompt as a new optional fenced `UI VERIFICATION` block. The reviewer task text is unchanged when no UI verification exists, and existing `prompts` and engine tests still pass unmodified. Payload text is bounded like the other evidence (tail and list caps).

Gates keep working without Playwright installed. `python -m pytest` (unit gate) and `ruff check .` pass in an environment that lacks Playwright and browsers: `tests/ui/` is excluded from default collection unless `DEVFLOW_UI_LANE=1` is set (via a `collect_ignore_glob` in `tests/conftest.py`), and Playwright is imported lazily or through `importorskip`. The configured integration gate `python -m pytest tests/test_engine.py tests/test_telemetry.py` also passes. The `[ui]` config section is documented. CI gets a separate `ui-lane` job that installs Playwright and chromium and runs the lane command, leaving the existing `test` job unchanged.

follow_ups.title: Render UI lane results and the Feature Use-Case Verification table in the devflow ui ticket drawer
follow_ups.why: The ticket drawer (`ui.py` `_gate_attempt`/`_review_section`) only shows backend gate results, so reviewers cannot see the lane outcome without opening the PR comment.

follow_ups.title: `devflow init` should detect frontend/UI surfaces and scaffold a `[ui]` config section
follow_ups.why: Without scaffolding, UI-touching diffs report the lane as 'unconfigured' until someone hand-writes `[ui]`, so the new lane stays dormant on most repos.

follow_ups.title: Cache the UI lane result by head sha between the GATES and IN_REVIEW stages
follow_ups.why: `_verify` runs once in `_gates` and again in `_in_review`, so a slow browser suite executes twice per ticket on the same commit.

follow_ups.title: Replace the loose Chrome screenshot check in `tests/test_ui.py::test_ui_server_and_e2e_browser` with the deterministic lane scenarios
follow_ups.why: The existing browser check only asserts that a screenshot file is larger than 1000 bytes, and it is skipped silently when no local Chrome is found.

plan.goal: Split gate verification into a backend lane (existing lint/unit/integration gates) and a UI lane. The UI lane activates when the diff touches user-facing files, runs a deterministic headless-browser suite against an ephemeral local server with no LLM driving, and fails on console warnings, JS errors and network 4xx/5xx. An LLM evaluator then maps the automation output to a planned 3–6 item use-case matrix and adds a structured 'Feature Use-Case Verification' table to the gate and review report. Without a `[ui]` config section, engine behaviour is unchanged.
out_of_scope: Rendering the UI lane results or use-case table inside the `devflow ui` ticket drawer (the payload keys are added; display is separate).
Auto-generating a `[ui]` section in `devflow init` or `detect.py` for repos with a frontend.
Adding `ui` to `detect.GATES` or baseline comparison of UI lane results.
A built-in generic server launcher for arbitrary stacks; the repo-supplied `[ui] command` owns server startup.
An LLM that drives the browser, or computer-use style interaction of any kind.
Editing the main checkout's `.devflow/config.toml`; enabling the lane on devflow's own tickets is an operator change documented in docs/ui-lane.md.
Allowlisting or ignoring known benign console warnings.
Caching the lane result across the gates and in-review passes.
risks: Dependency footprint: Playwright and its browser binaries are heavy and are not in `pyproject.toml`. The plan keeps them out of the default and `dev` extras and of the configured unit and integration gates, via lazy import, `importorskip` and `collect_ignore_glob`. If `tests/ui` leaked into default collection, `python -m pytest` would fail in environments without browsers, which is a gate regression.

Strict, un-baselined UI gating: console warnings, 4xx and 5xx all fail the lane, so a pre-existing warning in a repo's UI blocks every UI ticket until it is fixed. This follows the ticket's wording and is documented. An allowlist is deferred.

Public interfaces and contracts touched: `Config` (new `ui` field), `[ui]` TOML contract, `plan.schema.json` (additive), `test_plan`, `review.schema.json` (unchanged), `GateReport` (new optional `ui` field, used by `gates.run_gates`, `baseline.evaluate`/`report_to_dict`/`ensure_baseline`, `engine._verify`/`_evidence`/`_failure_text`/`_gates`/`_in_review`), `prompts.reviewer_task`/`planner_task` signatures (additive keyword arguments only), `config.PROMPTS`/`SCHEMAS`, the router's default roles, and the stage payload keys read by `ui.py`. Tests that exercise these and must be re-checked: tests/test_engine.py, tests/test_telemetry.py (the integration gate), tests/test_gates.py, tests/test_baseline.py, tests/test_loadconfig.py, tests/test_prompts.py, tests/test_router.py, tests/test_init.py, tests/test_ui.py. `Env` and `.engine()` in tests/test_engine.py have the most links in the graph, so extend them additively.

Repo-local copies of prompts and schemas under `.devflow/prompts` and `.devflow/schemas` shadow the shipped ones. Existing repos will not see the new planner/coder/evaluator instructions until `devflow init --force`. The engine-side validation of use cases (`uilane.validate_use_cases`) does not depend on the schema file, so enforcement still works, but the planner will not know to produce use cases. The loader should fail clearly if `ui_evaluator` prompt or schema is missing instead of crashing mid-ticket.

The graph shows only CI workflow nodes (`ci.yml`, `pages.yml`, `infra/langfuse/compose.yaml`) with no callers or tests for this slice. It is not a reliable guide to the Python callers, so the caller list above comes from reading `engine.py`, `gates.py`, `baseline.py`, `loadconfig.py` and `ui.py` directly. A stale graph could hide other callers of `_verify` and `GateReport`; the implementer should grep for them.

Determinism and flakiness: scenarios must use ephemeral port 0, a seeded store, no wall-clock sleeps (Playwright auto-wait and explicit locators only), and a fixed viewport. Screenshots and DOM artifacts are recorded as evidence but never compared pixel for pixel.

The evaluator is a second LLM call in IN_REVIEW and adds token cost only on UI tickets that pass the deterministic lane. It must stay advisory-plus-strict: it can add blockers but cannot turn a failing deterministic result into a pass (AC9).

Artifacts must be written outside the worktree (temp dir) so `gitops.commit_all` does not commit screenshots or reports, and report content fed to prompts must be bounded, since console text and DOM may contain untrusted page data. The evaluator prompt must fence it as data, not instructions.
Secrets: the lane command runs through `project_env`/`scrubbed_env`, so credentials are not exposed to browser-driven code. The `DEVFLOW_UI_*` variables carry only paths and a port.
CI runtime and flakiness: the new `ui-lane` job downloads chromium on each run. It is a separate job so it cannot break the existing `test` job, but it adds CI minutes.

steps.description: Add `UiCfg` (enabled, paths, command, timeout_minutes) to `Config`, parsed by a new `_ui(data)` in `load_config` from an optional `[ui]` table. `enabled` defaults to true when `command` is set. Validate types and raise `ConfigError` with a `[ui]` prefix. Defaults must not change any existing config's behaviour. Add loadconfig tests for absent, valid, and invalid sections.

Create `src/devflow/uilane.py`: `DEFAULT_UI_PATTERNS`, `touches_ui(files, patterns)`, a `UiCase`/`UiLaneReport` dataclass pair with `to_dict`, `load_report(path)` (strict parse), `free_port()`, `run_lane(cfg, worktree, plan_use_cases, timeout_s)`, and `validate_use_cases(plan, cfg)`. `run_lane` reuses `gates.run_command` and `gates.project_env` for process-group timeout and secret scrubbing, adds the `DEVFLOW_UI_*` env, creates a temp report/artifact dir outside the worktree so nothing untracked is committed, and applies the pass/fail rules from AC6. Also add `format_table(matrix, report, evaluation)` and `bounded_digest(report)`. Add `tests/test_uilane.py` covering AC1, AC3 validation, AC6 outcomes and the table output.

Add the deterministic runner support library `src/devflow/uirunner.py` as a pytest plugin/helper: a `ConsoleCollector` that subscribes to `console`, `pageerror`, `requestfailed` and `response` on a page-like object and exposes `errors()`, and a `ui_case(*use_case_ids)` marker. A `ui_page` fixture launches Playwright chromium headless (imported lazily), attaches the collector, fails the test at teardown if the collector has errors, and appends a case record (including a screenshot and DOM snapshot saved to `DEVFLOW_UI_ARTIFACTS`) to `DEVFLOW_UI_REPORT` when it is set. Test the collector with a fake page and no Playwright (AC5). Add a Playwright integration test guarded by `importorskip`.

Add `tests/ui/` scenarios for the `devflow ui` dashboard, each tagged with use-case ids. They boot `UiHandler` on port 0 against a seeded `tmp_path` store, reusing the seeding pattern from `tests/test_ui.py` (`seed`, `add`). Cover: happy-path board render and ticket card; opening the ticket drawer and the state persisting across reload; a deep link to a ticket; an error state (unknown ticket returns 404 in the drawer without an uncaught error); and a narrow viewport. Add `tests/ui/conftest.py` for the server fixture. Add `collect_ignore_glob` in `tests/conftest.py` so `tests/ui` is collected only when `DEVFLOW_UI_LANE=1`.

Extend the plan contract. Add the optional `ui_use_cases` property to `plan.schema.json` without changing existing required fields, so repo-local schema copies without it keep validating. Update `templates/planner.md` and `templates/coder.md` to instruct 3–6 use cases for UI tickets and the `ui_case` convention for scenarios. In `Engine._refining`, after `plan` is received with `status: ready`, call `uilane.validate_use_cases`. On violation, `_put` a `plan_feedback` and re-enter REFINING, bounded by the existing `MAX_PLAN_CYCLES`. Show use cases in `_format_plan`. Add `prompts.planner_task` guidance only when `[ui]` is configured.

Wire the lane into `Engine._verify`. After `run_gates` and `baseline.evaluate`, compute `gitops.diff_names(path, base_sha)`. If `[ui]` is enabled and `touches_ui` is true, run `uilane.run_lane`, store the result on `report.ui` (new optional field on `GateReport`, default None, so `baseline.report_to_dict` and the baseline cache are untouched), and fold failures into the verdict as `NewFailure(project='.', gate='ui', ...)`. Record an unconfigured lane in `verdict.unconfigured`. Extend `_evidence` with a bounded `ui_lane` entry, and `_failure_text` with case/error lines. Add `telemetry.event('gate.ui_lane', ...)` for ran/ok/duration/cases. `_verify` runs again at review time on the review worktree, so the lane runs twice per ticket just like the other gates. Add engine tests for the AC2/AC7 branches using a stub lane command.

Add the LLM evaluator. Create `templates/ui_evaluator.md` and `schemas/ui_evaluation.schema.json`. Register `ui_evaluator` in `config.PROMPTS` and `config.SCHEMAS` so `devflow init` copies them, and in `RoutingCfg.roles` defaults. Add `prompts.ui_evaluator_task(plan, criteria, digest)`. Add `Engine._ui_evaluation(t, review_wt, plan, ui_report)`, called from `_in_review` only when the lane ran and passed deterministically. It uses a dedicated `reviewer` agent when present, otherwise `run_routed` avoiding the coder's agent. It post-processes the result so any use case without a passing mapped case becomes `missing` (AC9), and converts fail/missing and blocking findings into blocking review findings that are merged into the existing `blocking` list.

Surface the verification table. Add an optional `ui_verification` argument to `prompts.reviewer_task` (the fenced block appears only when it is given) and to `Engine._format_review`. Store `ui_verification` (table text plus structured rows) in the `review` stage payload and `ui_lane` in the `gates` payload. The PR comment includes the table. Confirm the existing review and gates payload consumers (`ui.py` `_gate_attempt`, `_review_section`, `collect_ticket`) tolerate the new keys without rendering them, and add a test for that.

Documentation and CI. Add `docs/ui-lane.md` covering the `[ui]` config section (paths, command, timeout), the report contract, the `DEVFLOW_UI_*` env, the `ui_case` convention, the Playwright and browser install steps (suggested via project `setup`), and an example command: `DEVFLOW_UI_LANE=1 python -m pytest tests/ui -p devflow.uirunner`. Link it from README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md, noting that existing repos must run `devflow init --force` to pick up the new prompts and schemas. Add a `ui-lane` job to `.github/workflows/ci.yml` that installs Playwright with chromium and runs the lane command. Leave the existing `test` job as it is.

Verify with the configured gates: `ruff check .`, `python -m pytest`, and `python -m pytest tests/test_engine.py tests/test_telemetry.py`. Run them in an environment without Playwright to confirm the lane tests skip cleanly. Where Playwright is available, also run the lane command once with `DEVFLOW_UI_LANE=1` to confirm `tests/ui` passes and the report JSON validates through `uilane.load_report`.
