acceptance_criteria.text: GET /api/live returns 200 JSON with keys `now`, `runner` ({running: bool, pid: int|null}) and `runs` (a list). It never writes to the repository or creates `.devflow/state/devflow.db`: with no db it returns `runs: []`, and a request for /api/live?x=1 also resolves to the endpoint rather than a 404.

`runs` contains only tickets whose State is refining, test_design, implementing, gates or in_review. Tickets that are new, awaiting_*, changes_requested, escalated, merged or cancelled are excluded. Entries are ordered most recently updated first.

Each run has: issue, title, state, `node` (the stepper position, one of refine|plan|implement|gates|review), `completed_nodes` (the nodes before it), `stage_started_at`, `elapsed_s`, `agent` (raw name, display label, or null), `branch`, `worktree`, `commit` (short HEAD sha of the worktree, else the ticket's base_sha prefix, else null), `attempt` and `review_round`. The mapping is fixed: refining→Refine (01), test_design→Plan (02), implementing→Implement (03), gates→Verify Gates (04), in_review→Independent Review (05). A ticket sent back from gates to implementing shows Implement as active, with Refine and Plan checked.

`elapsed_s` is computed as now minus the timestamp of the ticket's latest `transition` event into the current state. It falls back to the ticket row's `updated_at` when there are no transition events, and is never negative.

Each run includes `benchmark` = {p50, p99, samples, stalled}. p50 and p99 come from `stall.percentile` over `stall.baseline_durations(read_log_records(traces.jsonl), 'stage.<state>')`. `stalled` is true only when samples >= stall.MIN_SAMPLES and elapsed_s > p99, matching `stall.check_stall`. With a missing or empty trace log, or fewer than MIN_SAMPLES, p50 and p99 are null and `stalled` is false, with no exception.

Each run includes `feed`: at most 20 entries, oldest to newest, each {ts, level (info|ok|fail), text}. Entries are derived from the ticket's events (transitions, errors) and stage_results (plan, gates per-command results like 'Gate: <cmd> ran in 1.4s (PASS)', review verdict). Raw agent `reply` text never appears.

The UI renders a sticky Flight Deck above the stats bar only while `runs` is non-empty. It shows the 5-node stepper (01 Refine, 02 Plan, 03 Implement, 04 Verify Gates, 05 Independent Review). Completed nodes have a green check badge, and the active node has an emerald glow pulse and animated connector. When there is more than one run, a '+N more' chip is shown.

The deck shows an agent pill (e.g. 'Claude Code', 'Codex', 'OpenClaw Planner'; the raw name when unknown; '—' when null), a worktree badge and a branch badge with the short commit. Clicking the worktree or branch copies the full value to the clipboard (navigator.clipboard, with a document.execCommand fallback) and shows brief 'Copied' feedback.

A mm:ss elapsed timer increments every second in the browser, anchored to the server's `elapsed_s` and the client's monotonic clock, so it is unaffected by client/server clock skew. It shows 'p50 mm:ss · p99 mm:ss' when benchmarks exist. When `stalled` is true the badge switches from emerald to amber with a gentle pulse and the text 'Stall Warning: Stage exceeding 99th percentile'. The timer also turns amber locally if the ticking elapsed value crosses p99 between polls.
A collapsible, terminal-style activity drawer shows the feed, with the newest entry last and scrolled to the bottom. Its open/closed state survives polling refreshes.

While an active run exists the page polls /api/live every 2–3 s, and at a slower idle rate otherwise. Requests never overlap (an in-flight guard) and an error leaves the last good view in place. Updates patch existing DOM nodes rather than rebuilding the page, the deck container keeps a reserved min-height while active, and focus and drawer state are preserved, so there is no full-page reload and no layout shift.

At a viewport of 640px or less the deck collapses into a compact banner (issue number, active stage, timer and stall badge), with the stepper reduced to a compact progress bar and the badge details hidden or collapsed. Animations are disabled under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

All dynamic strings (title, agent, branch, worktree, feed text) are HTML-escaped when rendered, and the existing /api/state, /api/ticket/<n>, board and inspector-drawer behaviour and tests are unchanged.

New tests in tests/test_ui.py cover AC1–AC13 (collect_live logic, the HTTP endpoint, and template markers). `ruff check .`, `python -m pytest` and `python -m pytest tests/test_engine.py tests/test_telemetry.py` all pass, and no existing test is weakened, skipped or deleted.

follow_ups.title: /api/state rejects query strings (404)
follow_ups.why: `do_GET` matches `self.path == "/api/state"` exactly while /api/ticket and /api/live parse the path, so `/api/state?x=1` or a cache-busting parameter returns 404 and the routing is inconsistent.

follow_ups.title: Record the active agent at stage start
follow_ups.why: agent_usage is written only after an agent call completes, so the live view cannot name the agent during the first (longest) call of a stage. Persisting a 'stage_started' or 'agent_started' event in the engine would make it exact.

follow_ups.title: Share one stage-latency baseline reader
follow_ups.why: `engine._stall_history` and the UI both re-read and parse the whole traces.jsonl on every call. A small cached/shared reader in stall.py would avoid O(file) work on every 2.5 s poll as traces grow.

plan.goal: Add a read-only GET /api/live endpoint and a sticky, auto-refreshing 'Live Flight Deck' at the top of the Devflow UI. For each in-flight ticket it shows the pipeline stage stepper, the active agent, worktree and branch with click-to-copy, a live elapsed timer compared with the stage's historical p50 and p99 (amber when over p99), and a collapsible feed of the last 20 engine events.
out_of_scope: WebSocket/SSE transport. Polling /api/live is sufficient, and the server is a stdlib ThreadingMixIn HTTPServer.
Changing engine behaviour, state transitions, the stall-check logic in engine.py/stall.py, or telemetry span emission, including emitting new live events from the engine.
New SQLite tables or schema migrations, or writes of any kind from the UI process.
A mid-stage live stall alert on stderr or in Langfuse. This is a UI-only indicator.
Changing the existing board columns, stats bar, ticket inspector drawer or /api/ticket payload.
Streaming raw agent output or terminal logs in the feed. Only sanitized engine/stage events are shown.
Per-agent or per-role p50/p99 benchmarks (stage-level only).
risks: Affected contracts and callers (graph slice is empty for ui.py, so this comes from reading the code): `UiHandler.do_GET`, `collect_state`, `collect_ticket`, `HTML_TEMPLATE` and `LIFECYCLE` are consumed by tests/test_ui.py (including `test_template_markers`, `test_markdown_is_inert`, `test_state_cards_gain_additive_fields` and the e2e browser test). Any change to the template or routing must keep those passing.

`Store` (75 graph links) and `State`/`Ticket` are core, widely-used types, and tests/test_engine.py and tests/test_telemetry.py exercise them (the integration gate). Store changes must be additive read-only methods with no schema change, and `Store(...)` opens the db with WAL plus `executescript`, so /api/live must keep the `db.exists()` guard to avoid creating state, as `collect_state` does.

Lock probing: `runner.ownership` holds an exclusive non-blocking flock on `<git-common-dir>/devflow-runner.lock`. Probing with flock from the UI could make a real run fail with RunnerBusy, so S2 uses pid liveness only. The pid file is not cleared on release, so a stale pid reused by an unrelated process can show `running: true`. Treat the runner flag as advisory and derive 'active' from ticket state, not from the lock.

The ticket names the states `planning` and `reviewing`, which don't exist. The real states are refining, test_design and in_review, with awaiting_plan_approval, awaiting_clarification and changes_requested as human/wait states. The plan fixes the mapping in AC3 and the active set in AC2, so the UI will not show the deck while a ticket waits on a human gate. Flag this if the product intent was different.

The ticket says to read latency statistics from `telemetry.py`, but the percentile and baseline helpers live in `stall.py`, and span names are `stage.<state>`. Benchmarks depend on `traces.jsonl` (`telemetry.log_path()` / `.devflow/state/traces.jsonl`) being present and holding at least MIN_SAMPLES (5) ok spans, and otherwise the stall radar stays off. Retry/changes_requested stages that reuse the `stage.implementing` span name share one baseline.

`git rev-parse` for each active worktree runs on every poll. Use a short timeout and no network, and degrade to base_sha or null if it fails. The feed is built from DB rows only, so it must never include agent `reply` text or secrets. Whitelist fields and run output through `_strip_reply`.

Frontend risk: the page is one inline string, so JS syntax errors are not caught by ruff. The e2e/template-marker tests and a manual browser check must cover it. Avoid `innerHTML` with unescaped values (XSS via ticket title or branch), avoid per-tick DOM rebuilds (layout shift or lost focus), and keep the drawer toggle state across polls.

Clock skew and timezone: `elapsed_s` is computed server-side and the client ticks from performance.now(), so the browser clock is never compared with DB timestamps. The timer can briefly lag by up to one poll interval after a tab is backgrounded (timers throttle), so it must re-anchor on every successful poll.

steps.description: Add small read-only accessors to Store: (a) the latest `transition` event timestamp per ticket (or a `ticket_updated_at(ticket_id)` accessor over tickets.updated_at) and (b) the latest agent_usage row for a ticket (agent, role, ts). The existing `events()`/`stage_results()` can cover the rest. Additive only: no schema change or migration, and existing signatures are untouched.

Add a read-only runner probe, `runner.runner_status(root)`. It resolves the git common dir, opens `devflow-runner.lock` read-only without creating it, reads the pid and checks liveness with os.kill(pid, 0), and returns {running, pid}. It must NOT acquire flock, which would contend with `ownership()` and could make a real run raise RunnerBusy. It tolerates a missing file, a garbage pid, a non-git root and PermissionError.

Add pure helpers to ui.py. `NODES` and `STATE_NODE` hold the fixed mapping from AC3, and `ACTIVE_STATES` is the five-state set. `AGENT_LABELS` maps claude→'Claude Code', codex→'Codex' and openclaw→'OpenClaw Planner' (raw name as the fallback). `_stage_benchmark(root, state, elapsed)` reuses `stall.percentile`, `stall.baseline_durations`, `stall.read_log_records` and `stall.MIN_SAMPLES`, reading `root/.devflow/state/traces.jsonl` (the same path `read_trace` uses) and treating span name `stage.<state.value>` as the key. `_feed(...)` builds the capped 20-entry list from events and stage_results via `_strip_reply`, extracting only whitelisted fields (state, actor, reason, error, per-command gate results, review verdict). `_head_sha(worktree)` runs `git rev-parse --short HEAD` with a short timeout and returns None if the path is missing or git fails.

Implement `collect_live(root, *, now=None)` in ui.py. It returns {now, runner, runs}, opens the db only if `state_db_path(root).exists()`, and never raises for a bad ticket (skip it and continue). Agent resolution order: (1) the latest agent_usage row for the ticket, (2) the matching stage payload's `agent` (implement/review) or `sessions['coder_agent']`, (3) null. Document in a code comment that the agent is unknown during the first call of a stage because usage is recorded after the call.

Route GET /api/live in `UiHandler.do_GET`: match on the parsed `path` (not the raw self.path), call `collect_live`, send it with `_json`, and return 500 {error} on an unexpected exception, mirroring `_ticket`. Leave /api/state, /api/ticket and / behaviour unchanged.

Add the Flight Deck markup and CSS to HTML_TEMPLATE, a sticky container placed before `.stats-bar` with a hidden/reserved-height default. The CSS covers the stepper, the emerald pulse keyframes and animated connector, the green check badges, the amber stall state, the agent/worktree/branch pills, the collapsible terminal drawer, a `@media (max-width: 640px)` compact banner, and `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`. Use the existing CSS variables and visual language, and add `aria-live="polite"` for stage changes only (not for the per-second timer).

Add the Flight Deck JavaScript to HTML_TEMPLATE. It uses a setTimeout-chained poller for /api/live (2.5 s when active, about 10 s when idle) with an in-flight guard and a keep-last-good-view error policy. `renderDeck(data)` patches existing nodes via textContent/classList and creates nodes only when the run set changes. A 1 s ticker updates only the timer text and amber state, using performance.now() deltas from the last fetch. The copy-to-clipboard handlers include a fallback and 'Copied' feedback. All dynamic values go through `escapeHtml`/textContent. Preserve drawer open state and scroll position (stick to the bottom only if it was already at the bottom). Clicking the deck's issue number opens the existing inspector via `openTicket`. The existing `fetchState`/`setInterval(fetchState, 3000)` stays, and the live-tracking label text is updated if it becomes inaccurate.

Add tests in tests/test_ui.py, reusing the existing `seed`, `add`, `serve` and `get` helpers. Unit tests: no-db returns empty runs and creates no db file; active/inactive state filtering; node mapping including gates→implementing retry; elapsed from the last transition and the updated_at fallback; benchmark with >=5 seeded `stage.<state>` spans (stalled true and false), <5 samples, a missing log and malformed lines; synthetic spans excluded; feed capped at 20, ordered, and containing no `reply` text; agent resolution order; a missing worktree doesn't crash; `runner_status` with no lock file, a garbage pid, a dead pid and the live pid (os.getpid()). Endpoint tests: /api/live and /api/live?x=1 return 200 JSON. Template-marker tests: '/api/live', the flight-deck element ids, the 640px media query, the reduced-motion query, the stall text and the copy handler. Run the existing `test_ui_server_and_e2e_browser` unchanged.

Check the docs. Grep README.md and docs/ for the UI/`devflow ui` and /api/state descriptions, and document /api/live and the flight deck (response shape, state-to-stage mapping, stall rule) where the UI is described. If the UI is not documented anywhere, add a short section to README.md.
Run the configured gates from the repo root and fix any failures without weakening tests: `ruff check .`, `python -m pytest`, `python -m pytest tests/test_engine.py tests/test_telemetry.py`.

review.reason: The plan is concrete, testable and grounded in the repo. I checked its main claims against the code. (1) `stall.py` has `percentile`, `baseline_durations`, `read_log_records` and `MIN_SAMPLES=5`. `check_stall` uses `elapsed > p99` with at least `MIN_SAMPLES` samples, so AC5 matches it. (2) The engine emits spans named `stage.<state.value>`, so the benchmark key is correct. (3) `runner.ownership` holds a non-blocking exclusive flock and writes the pid without clearing it on release. A read-only pid-liveness probe, as in S2, avoids contending with a real run, and the plan correctly treats the result as advisory. (4) `do_GET` does match `/api/state` on the raw `self.path` while `/api/ticket` uses the parsed path. Routing `/api/live` on the parsed path is correct, and the `/api/state` quirk is rightly left as a follow-up. (5) The real states are refining, test_design, implementing, gates and in_review. The ticket's 'planning' and 'reviewing' do not exist, and the plan fixes the mapping explicitly and flags this as a risk. Scope is bounded: additive read-only Store/runner helpers, no schema change, no writes from the UI process, and an `exists()` guard so the endpoint never creates the db. Escaping, no `reply` text in the feed, and the in-flight, no-layout-shift, reduced-motion and 640px requirements are specific. Verification covers all configured gates, including the integration gate `python -m pytest tests/test_engine.py tests/test_telemetry.py`, alongside lint and unit. Each acceptance criterion has a named test approach in S8. Two things for the implementer to watch. The ticket says benchmarks come from `telemetry.py`, but the plan uses `stall.py`, which is the right place. The agent is unknown during the first call of a stage, and the plan accepts and documents that.

acceptance_criteria.text: GET /api/runs returns JSON {"runs": [...], "total": N}. It includes only tickets in terminal states (merged, escalated, cancelled), newest completion first. Each run has: issue, title, state, outcome (merged | rejected_review | failed_gates | stalled | cancelled), outcome_label, pr_url (null when no PR), pr_number, started_at, completed_at, duration_s (null when unknown), implement_attempts, max_implement_attempts, review_rounds, agent, and blast {files, callers, symbols, uncovered, covered}.

Outcome classification is deterministic. MERGED -> merged. ESCALATED -> rejected_review if the last non-terminal stage reached was review-related (in_review/changes_requested/awaiting_merge_approval), failed_gates if it was gates/implementing/test_design, otherwise stalled. CANCELLED -> cancelled. Each branch is covered by a unit test.

duration_s is the completion timestamp minus the first transition-event timestamp for the ticket in SQLite (the terminal transition for completed_at, the earliest transition for started_at). A ticket with no transition events yields null duration and null timestamps without raising.

GET /api/runs on a repo with no devflow.db returns 200 with {"runs": [], "total": 0} and does not create .devflow/ or any state file. A broken row or an unreadable payload for one ticket does not fail the whole response.

The page has a segmented control with three buttons: Board View, Runs Ledger, Analytics (role=tablist/tab, aria-selected, keyboard-operable). Switching shows the matching panel without a page reload. The Board view keeps its current DOM ids (stats-bar, board-container), polling and drawer behaviour. The Analytics view shows a small summary computed client-side from /api/runs data (total runs, merged rate, median duration, average review rounds, counts per outcome).

The Runs Ledger renders a table with columns Ticket/PR (issue badge, title, PR link with a green PR icon when pr_url exists), Outcome badge, Duration & Timeline (human-readable duration plus completion timestamp), Iterations (pills such as '1/3' for implement attempts and 'N rounds' for review rounds), Blast Radius (files, callers, covered vs uncovered symbols) and Actions (Inspect button).

Clicking a row or its Inspect button opens the existing ticket drawer for that issue, using the existing openTicket(). Enter and Space on a focused row also open it. Clicking the PR link does not open the drawer.

A search box filters instantly, with no network request and no reload, by title substring (case-insensitive), issue number (with or without '#'), and agent name. Filter chips All Runs, Merged Only, Failed / Blocked (rejected_review, failed_gates, stalled, cancelled) and Multi-round Reviews (review_rounds >= 2) combine with the search text. Sorting by date, duration and review rounds toggles ascending/descending from the column headers.

Zero state: when there are no runs, or no runs match the filters, the table shows a clear empty message (distinct text for each case) rather than a blank table. Large histories: 50+ runs are paginated client-side (25 per page, prev/next and a 'showing X-Y of Z' label), and the page resets to 1 when the filter, search or sort changes.
An 'Export Runs JSON' button downloads the currently filtered and sorted runs as runs.json (Blob + download attribute) with no server round trip. It is disabled when there is nothing to export.

All ticket-derived strings inserted into ledger HTML go through escapeHtml, and PR/issue URLs go through safeUrl or are built from the repo slug. The page still loads no external scripts, stylesheets or fonts.

Existing behaviour is unchanged: /api/state and /api/ticket/<n> responses keep their shape, and all existing tests in tests/test_ui.py pass without being weakened or deleted. New tests cover collect_runs, the /api/runs endpoint and the new template markers. The configured gates pass: ruff check ., python -m pytest, and python -m pytest tests/test_engine.py tests/test_telemetry.py.

follow_ups.title: Record terminal reason and stall cause as a structured field
follow_ups.why: Ledger outcome is inferred from the previous state and free-text transition reasons, because events store only to/actor/reason. A structured outcome/failure_kind recorded by the engine at escalation would make 'Rejected (Review)' vs 'Failed (Gates)' vs 'Stalled' exact.

follow_ups.title: Add issue author to the ticket record
follow_ups.why: The ticket asks to search by author, but tickets only carry the coding agent and no issue author. Storing the author at pickup would allow true author search.

follow_ups.title: Full Analytics view (throughput, review-round distribution, cycle-time trends)
follow_ups.why: This ticket only ships a summary panel. Charts and trends need their own design and data aggregation.

follow_ups.title: Server-side pagination for /api/runs
follow_ups.why: The endpoint returns the full terminal history on every poll. That is fine for hundreds of runs but will not scale to thousands.

plan.goal: Add a Runs Ledger view to the Devflow UI, with a Board / Runs Ledger / Analytics view switcher, backed by a new read-only GET /api/runs endpoint. The ledger lists every finished ticket run (merged, rejected in review, failed gates, stalled) with search, filter chips, sorting, pagination, JSON export and an Inspect button that opens the existing ticket drawer.
out_of_scope: A full Analytics dashboard (charts, trends, cost/token breakdowns, Langfuse data). Only the lightweight summary in AC5 is in scope.
Changes to the Store schema, the engine, state machine transitions, or what the engine records (no new columns or events).
Server-side pagination, filtering or search; virtualized scrolling.
Fetching the issue author or issue metadata from GitHub for the ledger (no host calls in /api/runs).
Parsing traces.jsonl for run durations. SQLite transition events are the source of truth, and traces remain only in the existing per-ticket drawer.
Changes to the Board view, the ticket drawer contents, or the CLI `devflow ui` flags.
risks: Public interface: this adds a new HTTP contract (GET /api/runs). The /api/state and /api/ticket/<n> shapes must stay additive and unchanged. Existing callers affected are collect_state, collect_ticket and UiHandler.do_GET in src/devflow/ui.py, and the CLI `devflow ui` entry in src/devflow/cli.py (unchanged).

Test contracts: tests/test_ui.py has template-string assertions, including test_template_markers (drawer-overlay must come after board-container, no external src/stylesheet/@import) and test_markdown_is_inert, which slices HTML_TEMPLATE between 'function renderMarkdown', 'function chip(', 'function safeUrl' and 'function inlineMd'. Inserting JS inside those spans or renaming those functions will break the tests. New ids must not collide with board-container, drawer-overlay or dr-*.

Read-only state access: Store.__init__ creates the state directory and runs the schema, so collect_runs must check state_db_path(root).exists() first (as collect_ticket does). test_ticket_endpoint_without_db_does_not_create_state shows the contract. Store.list_tickets/events are also used by engine.py and the tests in tests/test_engine.py and tests/test_telemetry.py; do not change their signatures. The integration gate (tests/test_engine.py, tests/test_telemetry.py) should be run unchanged.

Outcome classification is heuristic, because the DB stores only the destination state and a free-text reason for each transition. Resumed or retried tickets, or tickets whose history was truncated, could be classified as 'stalled'. Mitigate by documenting the rules in code and testing every branch. Cancelled tickets get their own 'Cancelled' badge, which is not one of the four named in the ticket.
Author search: tickets carry no issue author, so search matches title, issue number and coding agent name. This is a deliberate deviation from the ticket text, tracked as a follow-up.

Durations: old tickets without transition events show an em dash instead of a duration. Tickets that were re-opened may report a duration that spans idle time, because it is wall-clock from the first event.

Polling: the ledger adds a /api/runs fetch every 3s while active. Re-rendering the table on each poll must preserve search text, focus, sort, page and scroll position. Skip the DOM update when the JSON is unchanged, as the drawer does with ticketJson.

XSS: titles and agent names come from issue text and tooling, so every interpolation must go through escapeHtml and every link through safeUrl. Add a test asserting a title containing is not emitted raw by the template helpers.
The Analytics view is under-specified in the ticket. A minimal summary is planned so that the toggle is not an empty page. Reviewers may want a richer view later.

steps.description: Add `collect_runs(root: Path) -> dict` to src/devflow/ui.py, next to collect_ticket. Return early with {runs: [], total: 0} when state_db_path(root) does not exist, mirroring collect_ticket, so no state is created. Open Store read-only in usage. Take terminal tickets from store.list_tickets(State.MERGED, State.ESCALATED, State.CANCELLED) and reverse them to get updated_at DESC. For each ticket read store.events(ticket.id, 'transition') for started_at, completed_at, duration_s and the last pre-terminal state used for classification, falling back to ticket.history entries when events are missing. Take the PR number from ticket.sessions.get('pr') and build pr_url with _repo_slug(root). Take the agent from the latest implement stage_result payload or sessions['coder_agent'], as collect_ticket does. Compute blast counts from the latest gates stage_result via the existing _blast_section(). Import the Limits default (max_implement_attempts) for the 'N/3' pill instead of hard-coding 3. Wrap per-ticket work in try/except so one bad row is skipped.

Add a small pure helper `_classify_outcome(ticket, transitions)` in ui.py implementing the AC2 rules, and a `RUN_OUTCOME_LABELS` map (Merged, Rejected (Review), Failed (Gates), Stalled, Cancelled). Keep it separate from LIFECYCLE so the board mapping is untouched.

Route `GET /api/runs` in UiHandler.do_GET. Match the path with urllib.parse (ignoring any query string), reuse the _json helper, and return 500 {error} on an unexpected exception like the other endpoints. Do not change the /api/state or /api/ticket handling.

Template markup and CSS in HTML_TEMPLATE. Add the segmented view switcher in the header area and wrap the existing stats-bar plus board-container in a board panel. Add a runs panel (search input, filter chips, sort header, table, pagination bar, Export button) and an analytics panel. Reuse the existing CSS variables, and keep the drawer-overlay element after board-container and the dark-green drawer palette markers asserted by test_template_markers. Add `@media` rules so the table scrolls horizontally on narrow screens.

Template JS. Add the following without inserting any function between 'function renderMarkdown' and 'function chip(' or between 'function safeUrl' and 'function inlineMd', because test_markdown_is_inert slices the template at those markers. acceptance_criteria.text: `GET /api/analytics?window=all|24h|7d` returns strict JSON (no NaN/Infinity) with these top-level keys: `window`, `generated_at`, `telemetry` (`{available, spans}`), `kpis`, `stages`, `bottleneck`, `stalls`, `friction`, `blast`. A missing or empty `window` means `all`. An unknown value returns HTTP 400 with `{error}`. The request never creates `.devflow/state` or the SQLite db.

`kpis` contains `median_cycle_seconds`, `first_pass_approval_rate`, `blast_short_circuit_rate` and `total_stalls`, each with its sample count. Each value is `null` (never 0) when there is no data. Median cycle time is the median of (first transition to merged transition) for tickets merged inside the window. First-pass rate is merged tickets with zero `changes_requested` transitions divided by merged tickets in the window. Short-circuit rate is `gate.order` events with `devflow.short_circuited` true divided by all `gate.order` events. `total_stalls` is the count of non-synthetic `stall.detected` events.

`stages` has an entry for each of Refining, Planning, Implementing, Gates and Review, in that order, built from `stage.*` spans. The mapping is refining→Refining, test_design→Planning, implementing and changes_requested→Implementing, gates→Gates, in_review→Review. `awaiting_*` spans are excluded as human wait. Each entry has `count`, `mean`, `p50`, `p90`, `p99` and `max` in seconds, or nulls with count 0. `low_samples` is true when count is below `stall.MIN_SAMPLES`. Synthetic and malformed records are ignored.
`bottleneck` names the stage with the largest p50 among stages with at least one sample, or null when none have samples. The UI visibly highlights that stage's bar and row.

`stalls` gives per-stage `count`, `rate` (stalls divided by that stage's span count) and `elevated` (true when count ≥ 1 and rate > 0.01). The UI renders a stall radar (SVG) in which elevated stages are visibly distinguished from normal ones, plus the total.

`friction` has `review` (`{blocking, nitpick, tickets}` totals over review findings, split by `blocking` truthiness) and `gate_failures` (top 10 `{label, count}` entries by frequency). Failure labels are taken from gate result fingerprints or failing commands. Labels are length-capped and passed through `telemetry.redact`. The UI renders both as a heatmap-style grid or bars.

`blast` has `avg_hop1_callers` (mean count of hop-1 callers per ticket impact) and `coverage_ratio` (modified symbols not in `uncovered`, divided by all impacted symbols, summed across tickets in the window). It also reports `tickets_with_impact`. Both values are `null` when no impact data exists. The UI displays them.

The `window` filter applies consistently. Spans and events are kept when `end_ns` is at or after now minus the window. Store-derived rows are kept when their `ts` is at or after that cutoff. `all` applies no filter.

The dashboard has an Analytics tab, reachable via the header nav and the `#analytics` hash and toggled against the Board. It holds the 4 KPI cards, the stage latency chart and table, the stall radar, the friction section, the blast section, and a 24h / 7d / All Time toggle. Durations display as `42s`, `2m 15s`, `8m 40s`. Null values display as `—`. Empty and no-telemetry states show an explanatory message, not a broken chart.

Rendering is fully offline. The HTML template adds no `<script src>`, `<link>`, `@import`, remote image, font or CDN reference. Charts are built with inline SVG using DOM APIs (`createElementNS` / `textContent`), and data values are never injected through `innerHTML` unescaped.

Existing behaviour is unchanged. The Board, flight deck, ticket drawer, `#ticket-N` deep links, `/api/state`, `/api/live`, `/api/ticket/*` and the `devflow telemetry metrics` output are untouched. All existing tests pass.

New unit tests cover the analytics computation, the endpoint (including 400, no-db and no-traces cases) and the template markers. `ruff check .`, `python -m pytest`, and `python -m pytest tests/test_engine.py tests/test_telemetry.py` all pass.
